note: E17a predictions from the v0.4 pycache calibration (N=1 baselines + class probes, sbx and resident-300, seeds 2,3,6,7 each) and three one-off guest diagnoses (grepcheck, grepdiag, hostcache; ~/e17-manifest.md on the rig). To be reviewed and sealed with the user before the first measured E17a rung. Summaries: e17/results/calibration/v0.4/.

calibration.host: AWS m7i.metal-24xl, 96 vCPU, 377 GiB, /srv/e15 XFS reflink, profile fresh-metal

latency_n1_seeded._: realistic turns, in-window ok calls; gain = 1 - resident-300 warm median / sbx median (e17/analysis/latency_report.py)

latency_n1_probes._: 20 back-to-back calls per class in one session (the first call is the workspace's first touch)

calibration.py_grep_mechanism: grep reads the venv's .py sources, which nothing else in a turn reads (imports load .pyc). Per call: (a) the first grep on a freshly copied workspace costs ~2 s in both arms (host page cache cold, new inode); (b) a later grep in the same lease VM costs ~115 ms (guest page cache); sbx gets ~390 ms from the host page cache; (c) a later grep in a NEW lease VM, after the previous one was idle-destroyed, cost ~2 s in the seeded runs but 0.49 s in the hostcache check, where the destroyed VM had run only two greps. Probable cause (not measured directly): each VM's cgroup has memory.max = PerVMBytes = guest RAM + overhead (remote-worker/internal/vmpool/cgroup.go writeMemoryMax), host page cache from a VM's own reads is charged to it, and a lease VM that ran analyze/pytest sits at ~1024 MiB (every resident-300 VM peaked at 1023.98 MiB), so its charged host cache is reclaimed. This is not specific to the E15 resident patch: the shipped lease runs in the same per-VM cgroups.

py_grep_case_shares._: from the pycache corpus gaps (a VM survives between two calls iff the gap <= the idle timeout)

predictions.claim: Spec §7.5 criterion 2 FAILS at pycache on the resident patch: lease-300's warm py_short gain is >= 0.50, but py_import's and py_grep's are below 0.50, at N=1 and at N=128. Predicted gains (lease-300, per class): py_short [0.75, 0.95]; py_import [0.25, 0.50); py_grep below 0 (lease warm median in [1500, 2500] ms against an sbx median in [300, 700] ms); py_analyze [-0.05, 0.15] and py_test [-0.05, 0.05] (reported, not gated). So E17a misses and goes back to the user before the build (spec §7.5).
predictions.metric: e17/analysis/latency_report.py gain per class, point pycache, N=1 and N=128, arms sbx and lease-300 (= resident-300)
predictions.falsifiedBy: any gated class's gain >= 0.50 where predicted below, or below 0.50 where predicted above, at either N (the verdict part); separately, a gain outside its range falsifies the numeric part
predictions.note: py_import: about 450 ms of a warm import is Python unpacking and initialising numpy/pandas/scipy/sklearn, which no cache removes; the lease saves only sbx's ~300 ms of fresh VM plus cold guest page cache. pytest imports the same stack just before py_import in a turn, so py_import is warm whenever the VM survives (~90% at 300 s). py_grep: with 300 s, about 68% of greps are case (a) or (c), each ~2 s, so the lease median lands on ~2 s while sbx's lands on its host-cached ~390 ms (calibration_n1_seeded shows sbx 1960 ms only because 3 of its 5 in-window greps were first-on-workspace). At N=128 host CPU contention adds to every arm alike; sbx's standby depth 2 may not cover concurrent short Execs, which can only raise py_short's gain.

predictions.claim: At point default (9.5% duty, the E15 trace corpus) the E15 metal ordering repeats: sbx N_max in [64, 96]; lease-300 N_max in [112, 160]; lease-120 in [96, 160]; lease-30 in [64, 128]; lease-300 >= sbx by at least one ladder step, so criterion 1 holds.
predictions.metric: assembled ladder.json n_max per arm at point default (primary verdict, E15 §8 / E16 §7.1 rules)
predictions.falsifiedBy: n_max(lease-300) < n_max(sbx) (criterion 1 fails); separately, any arm's n_max outside its range
predictions.note: E15 metal on this host: sbx 80, resident-300 128, resident inf 128, every arm failing on the condition-4 p95 tail of long CPU-heavy calls. lease-300 here is the same resident patch at the same idle timeout. lease-30 keeps no standby (depth 0), so most Execs pay a cold boot sbx's standbys hide; it can land at or below sbx.

predictions.claim: lease-30 loses most of the warm share: its warm share at pycache is in [0.50, 0.70] (lease-120 [0.78, 0.90], lease-300 [0.86, 0.95]), and its first-call-after-idle py_short median is at or above sbx's py_short median.
predictions.metric: latency_report.py warm_share and first_after_idle per arm, point pycache, N=1 and N=128
predictions.falsifiedBy: lease-30 warm share above 0.70 or below 0.50; or its first-after-idle py_short median below sbx's
predictions.note: The corpus gaps decide the warm share: median gap 18 s, p75 61 s, p90 234 s; 60% / 85% / 91% of calls follow a gap within 30 / 120 / 300 s. A lease VM recreated after idle has no standby behind it, so its first call pays a full VM start.

predictions.claim: Lease VMs at pycache reach their cgroup ceiling: at least 80% of lease-300 VMs peak above 900 MiB (guest RAM 1024 MiB), at N=1 and at N=128; median peak in [950, 1024] MiB.
predictions.metric: per-VM peak of samples.jsonl vm_mem (memory.current of the VM cgroup) over the rung, arm lease-300, point pycache
predictions.falsifiedBy: fewer than 80% of lease-300 VMs above 900 MiB, or a median peak below 950 MiB
predictions.note: analyze.py reads the 256 MiB dataset and builds a pandas frame plus a KMeans fit in one call; the guest keeps its page cache and the host never gets the freed pages back (no balloon, lease spec decision 7). In the calibration every resident-300 VM peaked at 1023.98 MiB. This is the growth question 3 asks about; with a 1024 MiB guest the lease VM is effectively charged its full guest RAM after the first analyze.

predictions.claim: (E17b only) Level 1's end-of-Exec kill, fresh shell and privilege drop add [2, 50] ms per Exec at N=1, measured as lease-300 (shipped) against the E17a resident patch on the default probe classes.
predictions.metric: spec §7.4: N=1 per-call added latency, class medians, shipped lease-300 minus resident patch
predictions.falsifiedBy: a median added latency outside [2, 50] ms
predictions.note: No E17b measurement exists yet; the range is wide on purpose and is the only prediction here without calibration data.

predictions.claim: The driver stays under 1% of host CPU (A2) on every E17a rung.
predictions.metric: driver-cpu.jsonl per rung: driver CPU / (96 vCPU x window)
predictions.falsifiedBy: any E17a rung with driver CPU >= 1% of host CPU
predictions.note: E15 and E16 held A2 up to N=1536 on this host with the same driver; pycache's call rate per session is lower than the trace corpus's.

open_for_the_seal: Criterion 2 is predicted to fail (prediction 1). Keep the 50% bar as decided (2026-11-11) and let the rungs confirm it, or decide now that the calibration answers E17a's latency question.

py_grep's case (c) cost (~2 s) rests on a probable cause, per-VM memory.max reclaiming a grown lease VM's host page cache, that was not measured directly. If it is wrong, the lease's py_grep median moves toward ~0.5 s, still below sbx's, so prediction 1's verdict does not depend on it.

Lease design input, whatever E17a's verdict: with memory.max = guest RAM + overhead, a lease VM that fills its guest RAM loses its host-cached workspace pages, so the VM that replaces it starts colder than a per-Exec VM would.
sealNote: Sealed on the user's go-ahead (2026-11-12, 'go ahead with the recommendation'), before any measured E17a rung. User decision at the seal: the 50% criterion-2 bar stays; the E17a latency matrix is cut to one rung pair, point pycache N=128, sbx and lease-300 (= resident-300), because the N=1 calibration already answers the latency question at N=1 and N=128 is the one case that could move it. Criterion 1 reuses E15's metal default ladders (sbx 80, resident-300 128) if the driver, corpus and rig profile match, otherwise runs those two arms only. pycache-low, the gain-against-D runs, the 256 MiB guest-RAM runs and the lease-30/lease-120 ladders are not run in E17a. Predictions 1-6 are unchanged; their N=1 parts are judged on the calibration, their N=128 parts on the new rung pair.
